POLICY & PROCEDURE FOR RATIONAL USE OF BLOOD AND BLOOD PRODUCTS:

1. POLICY:

  • Blood and blood products shall be used rationally and only on advice of the consultant.
  • Informed consent shall be obtained whenever use of blood or blood products is transfused.
  • Transfusion service is followed as per Indian Drug Control Act.
  • The Blood / Blood Product Requisition Form must be filled by on duty concern RMO only.
  • The Blood or Blood Products except platelets and FFP should always be transported in blood containers (Ice Box).
  • Platelets & FFP will be transported at room temperature in closed container.
  • The blood and blood products are procured from Blood Bank- the empanelled outsourced blood bank.
  • Patient’s NOK may bring the blood or blood product form any government blood bank or our empanelled outsourced blood bank. Bank Personnel will supply the blood product to the hospital.

2. PURPOSE:

To ensure that transfusion of blood and blood products carried out effectively and safely by trained personnel in accordance with the provisions of the Drug and Cosmetics Act.

3. SCOPE:

All Patients need transfusion of blood and blood products.

4. RESPONSIBILITY:

Primary consultant, Concern RMO, Surgeon and/or Anesthetist (only surgery cases), Nurse, out sourced blood bank.

5. DISTRIBUTION:

Wards, ICU, Operation Theaters.

6. PROCEDURE:

The requisition for Blood and its products e.g., Whole Blood, concentrated RBCs , Platelets, Fresh Frozen plasma (FFP), Platelets rich plasma (PRP) is made as per the primary consultant’s advice depending upon the status of admitted patients and emergency cases. The condition where blood and blood product can be used is included but not limited in the followings-

6.1 Indications for transfusion in adults:

6.1.1 Conditions where whole blood transfusion is required:

  • Sudden loss of blood volume.
  • Major surgery.

6.1.2 Conditions where Packed Red Blood Cells transfusion is required:

  • In symptomatic anaemia – who require increased Oxygen carrying capacity
  • Decreased bone marrow production – like leukemia
  • In decreased red cell survival conditions like haemolytic anaemia
  • In bleeding patient, surgical or traumatic.

6.1.3 Conditions where platelets transfusion is required:

  • Reduced platelet count with active bleeding.
  • Persistent reduced/ decreasing platelet count not responding to other measures with risk of impending bleeding manifestation.

Note: Single donor platelet preferred over random donor platelet.

6.1.4 Conditions where Fresh Frozen plasma (FFP) transfusion is required:

  • Congenital or Acquired coagulation factor deficiencies.
  • Prolonged INR with bleeding tendencies due to anticoagulant dosage maladjustments.

6.3 List of situations where emergency blood transfusion required:

  • Sudden loss of blood volume
  • Pre-op Hb < 8 gm, % in major blood loss surgery
  • Hb< 9 g/dl in chronic transfusion regimen

PROCEDURES GOVERN TRANSFUSION OF BLOOD AND BLOOD PRODUCT:

1. Initial checks:

  • The past and present health status of the patient is assessed.
  • The history of blood transfusions in the last six months is assessed.
  • The patient’s body weight is checked.
  • The patient’s vital parameters are monitored.

2. Pre-procedure:

  • It is confirmed that transfusion has been prescribed by primary consultant.
  • Blood is collected for cross matching, grouping.
  • The patient/patient’s NOK is informed regarding the need for blood transfusion.
  • Informed consent is obtained from the patient/patient’s NOK.
  • The procedure is explained to the patient/patient’s NOK.
  • The patient is educated to recognize signs and symptoms of transfusion reaction (itching, swelling, fever, chilliness).
  • The patient’s vital parameters are monitored to establish a baseline for comparing vital signs during transfusion.
  • It is ensured that pre-medication given to the patient before transfusion if administered.
  • Blood/blood products are obtained from the hospital’s empanelled outsourced blood bank if it is arranged by the blood bank.
  • Blood and blood products transports in insulated container to location and delivers it to nurse in charge / staff nurse from blood bank. Signs, date, time of receives is document it in blood requisition form.
  • The patient’s identity is double-checked by asking for the patient’s name and check patient’s registration number. This is counter-checked with the ID band.
  • The patient’s Blood group, the date of collection, the date of expiry is also checked.
  • The patient’s privacy is maintained.

3. Intra-procedure:

  • The blood to be transfused is checked for gas bubbles, abnormal colour, cloudiness or clots by the concern RMO and then double checked by the allocated nurse.
  • Sterile blood transfusion set is kept ready for transfusion procedure.
  • Blood is brought to the room temperature.
  • Hand hygiene is followed and gloves are worn as standard precautions.
  • A venflon is put and the patency is assessed.
  • The IV channel is secured.
  • Pre medication is given before transfusion if ordered by the primary consultant/RMO.
  • Blood is administered to the patient following the 7 Rights and desired calculated rate following-
      • Right patient
      • Right time
      • Right route
      • Right dose
      • Right blood/blood product as ordered
      • Right documentation (in blood transfusion record)
  • The vital signs are checked after five minutes of starting the transfusion.
  • Vital signs are monitored at regular intervals: every 15 minutes for the first half-an-hour and then hourly till the transfusion lasts.
  • Rate of transfusion:
  • Adults; Start with 1 ml/min for first 15 minutes. If no reaction, increase to 4ml/minutes after 15 minutes.
  • For Pediatric Transfusions, take advice of Treating Pediatrician.
  • If patient shows evidence of a transfusion reaction immediately discontinue the transfusion at cannula hub and inform the on duty RMO and follow the hospital protocol.
  • It is ensured that transfusion is initiated and completed in the prescribed time.
  • After transfusion, the line is flushed with normal saline.
  • Post –Procedure:
  • Vital signs are monitored and compared with baseline data.
  • Used materials are disposed in accordance with the infection control policy (see Infection Control Manual).
  • The execution of the procedure is documented legibly in the patient’s medical record by the concern RMO.
  • The patient is monitored for response to the procedure and its effectiveness, as directed by the primary physician.
  • Document the following in blood transfusion record :
      • Amount of blood transfused
      • Blood unit and blood bag number
      • Start and finish time of transfusion
  • In case of transfusion reaction, analysis is done for corrective and preventive actions.

Addition of Drugs:

  • Exception: Normal saline, 5% albumin.
  • Addition of drugs may cause a change in the blood e.g. ringers lactate results in clotting of blood and is contraindicated along with blood.
  • Dextrose 5% results in haemolysis.
  • Changes in drug can occur because of Ph & ionic molecular constituent.
  • Flow chart in case blood transfusion reaction occurred:

Blood transfusion reaction occurs.

Stop the blood transfusion.

Immediately inform RMO & give treatment as per the requirement of the patient.

Remove blood bag with BT set.

Draw blood sample from the opposite hand.

The transfusion reaction detail is written by the RMO in the hospital letter head.Send to Blood Bank

Make a Xerox of cross match paper.

Urine for RE send to hospital pathology.

Document Transfusion reaction details and action taken in the in the Blood Transfusion Record Form and kept in the patient medical record with duly signed by the Sister-in-charge.

Filled up incident form (and the original copy is send to the Quality Assurance Department and a Xerox copy is kept with the concerned ward.

Received rechecked cross match paper from the blood bank and original kept in the patient medical record.

  • Relevant information regarding blood transfusion:
  • Transfusion services are governed by applicable laws/regulations.
  • Blood and blood products should be taken from licensed blood banks.
  • Informed consent is necessary for donation and transfusion of blood and blood products. This includes information on risks, benefits, alternatives, reason for the transfusion and also educating the patient and family on donation
  • The RMO /Consultant should take consent and sign the Consent Form.
  • For babies and pediatric patients, parents or next of kin/legal guardian should give consent and sign the Consent Form.
  • In case there is an emergency or a life-saving situation or where the patient is unaccompanied, the treating doctor should document this in the file.
  • Properly labeled samples should be given for grouping and cross-matching.
  • Before transfusion, the blood or blood products should be checked by the Nursing Staff and the RMO.
  • A blood product should be used as quickly as possible or, if the blood product so permits, stored in a designated fridge.
  • Blood products are generally infused via peripheral venous access. They may also be administered via central venous line.
  • Blood or blood product administration should be documented by the concern RMO. It should include starting time, volume to be transfused, duration of transfusion and patient’s response to the transfusion.

Policy of Return and discard of expired blood component –

        • If Blood component is not required for patient, it should be immediately returned to blood bank. Within 30 mins maintaining appropriate temperature.
        • If transportation period exceeds to 30 minutes, blood unit should be discarded in following manner.

Collect the Bag → Autoclave the bag on 121*C for 60 minutes → After autoclave, discard the bag in yellow colour coded bean

Blood Transfusion Committee composition & Meeting frequency:

Purpose

To promote safe and effective good transfusion practices in hospital in accordance with the Institutional, national or international benchmarks for the blood, blood components and associated blood products.

2.0 Scope:2.0 Scope:

Applicable to all units of WH

3.0 Frequency of meeting:3.0 Frequency of meeting:

Quarterly

4.0 Functions:4.0 Functions:

    • To establish and monitor broad policies for blood transfusion therapy such as: informed

consent, monitoring, Blood transfusion reactions etc. in keeping with the law of the land.

    • To review performance of outsourced blood bank in areas such as response to requests, productivity and outdating of components and improve quality of patient care by assessment of the on-going transfusion services, by reviewing and analysing the statistical reports of the transfusion services as well as promoting appropriate use of various blood administration devices.
    • To assist the blood transfusion services in blood bank in blood procurement efforts, assessing the adequacy and safety of the blood supply.
    • To audit use of whole blood, components, reactions and occurrence of events of the post transfusion reactions.
    • To review blood bank proficiency testing, accreditation reports and quality control results along with staff education.
    • To make provision for an active forum to facilitate communication between those involved with transfusion.
    • To report, monitor and follow up of adverse reactions to transfusion.
    • To develop and review institutional policies and systems.
    • To identify staff training requirements in clinical and laboratory transfusion practices.
    • To develop local educational and training materials as required.
    • To Collect and monitor blood ordering practices, use and wastage statistics, errors and incidents.
    • To identify problems in any aspect of blood transfusion including the delivery of services by the National Blood Transfusion Council and areas where guidance or additional resources are needed.
    • To promote non-clinical hospital liaison activities e.g. the blood stocks management and interaction with the other such groups
    • To identify and respond to patient’s perceptions about the provision of transfusion services.
    • Formulating policies & guidelines for use of blood and blood components
    • Establishing Standard Surgical Blood Ordering Schedules (SSBOS)
    • Monitoring source and supply of blood components

Agenda:

    • Review of previous minutes of meeting
    • Review of blood transfusion related incidences and status of corrective and preventive action
    • Review of Quality indicators related to blood transfusions
    • Review of quality improvement projects identified and status update
    • Other subjects if any as decided by Unit Head

Terms of office of the committee:

    • The committee will be appointed for a period of two years. The members of the committee shall hold office for a period of two years from the date of appointment.
    • The management of SNH will have the right to reappoint all or any of the said members and appoint new members and/or to fill any vacancy, howsoever caused.

Records to be maintained and the retention period:

    • Minutes of meeting
    • Incidence forms with RCA-CAPA
    • Quality indicators analysis

The records shall be maintained for a period of 5 years
